paper.quote: conspicuous horizontal and vertical strips, rather than diagonal or curved patterns
paper.plain: The learned patterns run along rows and columns. Shapes with straight, axis-aligned sides would produce this, and round or slanted shapes would not.

paper.say: The model says the patterns the network can paint are mostly straight horizontal and vertical lines, with few diagonals or curves.

paper.quote: these pixels are all in column 2, at successive rows.
paper.plain: Unit 0 of the first layer responds to bright pixels stacked in column 2, so it looks for something vertical there.

paper.say: The model says the pixels this part of the network watches are stacked in one vertical line, in column 2.

paper.quote: Output unit 55 has a strong horizontal strip at row 1
paper.plain: When this hidden unit is active it brightens row 1 and barely touches row 2. It marks a horizontal edge at that exact height.

check.note: Weights match, and on clean filled squares at t=20 unit 55 fires only when the top edge is at row 1 (mean 2.8, 0 otherwise).

paper.say: The model says one pattern is a bright horizontal line near the top of the image, on row 1.

paper.quote: Output unit 57 has a strong vertical strip at column 8
paper.plain: This unit brightens column 8 and darkens column 9 beside it. That pair draws a sharp vertical boundary between the two columns.

check.note: Weights match, and unit 57 fires on clean filled squares only when the right edge is at column 8 (mean 2.0, 0 otherwise).

paper.say: The model says another pattern is a bright vertical line at column 8, toward the right of the image.

paper.quote: Other units place strips elsewhere: unit 47 emphasizes row 3; unit 56 emphasizes column 10
paper.plain: Different units draw the same kind of line at different positions. The model keeps a separate unit for each place an edge can sit.

check.note: Unit 47 peaks on row 3 at 0.44, and unit 56 peaks on column 10 and fires for a right edge at column 10.

paper.say: The model says other patterns put similar lines in other places, such as row 3 and column 10.

paper.quote: The output bias favors dark margins
paper.plain: With every hidden unit silent, the output is the bias b3. The corners sit near -0.7, close to black, so shapes stay away from the border.

check.note: Corner values match; mean |b3| is 0.41 on the outer ring and 0.06 on rows and columns 2 to 9.

paper.say: The model says the network's starting values keep the outer edge of the image dark.

paper.quote: These structures favor axis-aligned boxes with variable edge positions.
paper.plain: Lines along rows and columns at many positions fit a box whose sides can move. This is the step that selects the square family.

check.note: The model's samples are axis-aligned boxes, with edges found on every row and column from 1 to 10 across 100 generated images.

paper.say: The model says these lines fit rectangles with sides parallel to the image edges, and those sides can sit in different places.

paper.quote: Narrow strips, sometimes with opposite-sign weights immediately alongside them, suggest thin outlines more than solid filled regions.
paper.plain: The answer reads a thin output pattern as a thin line in the image. A thin bright and dark pair also fits a solid square, where it marks where the fill stops.

check.note: Unit 57 fires for solid squares ending at column 8, and it turns column 8 on and column 9 off; many other units paint the interior.

paper.say: The model says thin lines, sometimes with a dark line right beside them, suggest thin outlines more than solid shapes.

paper.quote: white, approximately one-pixel-thick rectangular outlines on black
paper.plain: This is the final answer: a hollow box. The trained images are solid squares, so the box family is right and the interior is wrong.

check.note: All 8 stored samples and all 100 we generated by running the model are solid white squares, with every interior pixel white.

paper.say: The model says its best reading is white rectangle outlines, about one pixel thick, on black.

astra.plain: A negative line darkens a column when its unit is active. Here column 3 is pushed to black.

astra.quote: The four corner output biases are
astra.plain: The bias b3 is the output when no hidden unit is active. Values near -0.7 at the corners mean those pixels start close to black.

astra.quote: This favors variable-sized, axis-aligned boxes rather than circles, diagonal figures, handwriting, or unstructured textures.
astra.plain: The straight lines exclude round and slanted shapes. Their many positions mean the box moves or changes size from image to image.

check.note: The paper's classifier calls 98.4% of 1,000 samples squares, and our 100 samples show sides of 4 to 8 pixels at varying positions.

astra.say: The model says this points to straight-sided boxes of different sizes, and away from circles, diagonal figures, handwriting or random textures.

astra.quote: The narrow stripes, rather than predominantly solid rectangular patches, suggest outlines rather than filled rectangles.
astra.plain: This is the turning point of the answer. Thin weight patterns are taken to mean thin lines in the image, though a unit can also record where a solid shape's edge sits.

check.note: Units 55 and 57 fire on solid test squares with an edge on their line, and a hollow test image gets interior predictions near +0.2 against +1.1 for a filled one.

astra.say: The model says the thin lines, with few solid patches, suggest outlines more than filled rectangles.

claude.quote: the outer ring of pixels is strongly negative, meaning those pixels default to black.
claude.plain: The bias b3 is the output with all hidden units silent. A strongly negative ring keeps the border black, so shapes must fit inside it.

claude.quote: Filled blobs or filled rectangles would instead show broad regions
claude.plain: This is the key inference: a filled shape should appear as filled patches in the weights. A network can instead use thin units to record edge positions and add up a fill from many units.

claude.say: The model says that if the shapes were filled, it would expect to see large solid patches in the weights.

claude.quote: with a dark interior between the sides. That is a hollow rectangle.
claude.plain: The claim is that the middle of these patterns stays dark. A value near zero in W3 only means the unit leaves that pixel alone, and other units can still paint it white.
